hypothesis: Filtering trades to only days with daily range > 300 pts will significantly improve Sharpe ratio and average P&L per trade while maintaining positive total returns.
notes: EXP-0002 found avg P&L: <200pts=-₹53, 200-300=+₹97, 300-400=+₹277, 400-600=+₹604. Test: skip days with opening daily range estimate < 300 pts. Use prior-day range as proxy for current-day range (no look-ahead). Baseline: EXP-0001 corrected result (+376%, 532 trades, 32.1% WR).
conclusion: HYPOTHESIS PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. Range filter (>300pts prior-day) improves avg P&L per trade by +21% (₹141→₹171) but reduces total returns from +376% to +142% because 96% of July days are filtered out, eliminating a profitable month entirely. The filter is too aggressive with a single hard threshold. FINDING: The range/ATR relationship is monotonic up to 600 pts but a hard binary filter destroys value in low-range months that still have profitable setups. NEXT: Test softer regime-weighting (position size scaling) rather than hard binary filter.
next_steps: EXP-0005: ATR-based position scaling (scale lots by ATR ratio, not binary cut)
EXP-0004: Near-expiry sub-strategy still valuable regardless of this result
